title: Hybrid metaheuristic optimization of convolutional neural networks for tomato leaf disease classification
task: CNN hyperparameter optimization for plant disease classification
key_results: ALO-DA achieved 97.83% test accuracy; hybrid metaheuristics outperformed single optimizers on tomato leaf disease dataset (21,421 training images, 10 classes)
comments: Hybrid metaheuristic approach is sensible but the comparison lacks ablation studies showing which optimizer components contribute most to performance gains.

inputs: Tomato leaf images (21,421 training, 4,586 validation, 4,602 test)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hybrid metaheuristics balance exploration-exploitation better than single optimizers for CNN hyperparameter tuning
hypotheses.result: ALO-DA, ALO-WOA, PSO-WOA achieved 97.83%, 97.67%, 97.52% respectively; ALO-PSO achieved 95.26%

title: Spatial scaling of metagenomic diversity reveals ecological disruption in the gut microbiome of gout patients
task: Characterizing gut microbiome dysbiosis in gout using spatial scaling diversity metrics
key_results: Gout microbiomes showed higher inter-individual dissimilarity (z-values) for rare genes but weaker scaling for dominant genes; maximal accrual diversity (MAD) substantially lower in gout patients; CAZy enzyme diversity increased while KEGG metabolic pathways decreased
comments: Novel m-DAR framework provides ecologically nuanced dysbiosis characterization, but mechanistic links between observed diversity patterns and gout pathogenesis remain speculative.

inputs: Gut microbiome samples (gout patients, healthy controls)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Gout is characterized by loss of ecological structure in gut microbiome reflected in altered scaling patterns
hypotheses.result: Gout microbiomes exhibit greater inter-individual dissimilarity at rare gene level, weaker dominant gene scaling, and constrained total gene diversity potential

hypotheses.hypothesis: Functional dysbiosis in gout involves perturbed metabolic capacity
hypotheses.result: Increased CAZy scaling but decreased KEGG/KO pathway scaling in gout microbiomes

title: SwiftMSeg: lightweight multi-scale local–global context modeling with transformer for medical image segmentation
task: Lightweight medical image segmentation across multiple modalities
key_results: SwiftMSeg achieved Dice scores of 0.896 (colonoscopy), 0.860 (pathology), 0.850 (ultrasound), 0.870 (MRI) with 4.48M parameters (~53× fewer than U-Net); Hausdorff distances 16.43 (MRI) and 33.89 (ultrasound)
comments: Strong generalization across diverse imaging modalities with efficient architecture; domain-independent performance claims warrant external validation on truly independent datasets.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Transformer-based local-global-local module combined with hierarchical multi-scale decoder improves boundary localization and context modeling
hypotheses.result: Significant improvements in Dice scores (p<0.001) and lower Hausdorff distances across all modalities compared to baselines

title: Hybrid CNN BiLSTM architecture for smart grid cyberattack detection using smart meter data
task: Real-time cyberattack detection in smart grids via CNN-BiLSTM with ensemble decision
key_results: 92.17% accuracy (±0.27%), 90.58% precision (±0.49%), 81.24% recall (±0.86%), 85.66% F1-score (±0.20%), 95.60% ROC-AUC (±0.14%); 12 ms inference latency on 72,073 labeled power-grid logs
comments: Comprehensive class-imbalance mitigation and ablation studies strengthen confidence; bidirectional processing yields 20.12 pp accuracy gain over unidirectional LSTM, and Extra Trees head adds 10.09 pp precision over standalone.

inputs: 128-dimensional smart meter measurements (voltage, current, frequency harmonics)

hypotheses.hypothesis: BiLSTM captures temporal attack-evolution patterns better than unidirectional LSTM
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: bidirectional processing increased accuracy by 20.12 pp over unidirectional CNN-LSTM

hypotheses.hypothesis: Extra Trees ensemble head improves robustness over softmax layer
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Extra Trees boosted precision by 10.09 pp over standalone Extra Trees baseline

hypotheses.hypothesis: Weighted-learning strategy optimally balances class imbalance (2.49:1 ratio)
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: weighted learning is Pareto-optimal vs. 9 alternative imbalance strategies; statistical significance (p < 0.001) verified via McNemar's tests

title: A fractal-enhanced deep learning framework for forecasting agricultural production in India
task: Agricultural production forecasting via fractal-augmented LSTM/Bi-LSTM
key_results: LSTM with variable-scaling FIF achieved MAPE of 1.70% (Wheat), 1.95% (Maize), 5.06% (Millet); Bi-LSTM achieved 1.39% (Rice); variable-scaling FIF produced Hurst exponent 0.777–0.875 vs. constant scaling
comments: Fractal interpolation as a preprocessing step is sensible for volatile time series, though the marginal gain over simpler augmentation techniques is not quantified.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Variable-scaling FIF captures non-smooth features better than constant-scaling FIF
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: rougher interpolation (higher fractal dimension 1.153–1.574) improved LSTM accuracy

hypotheses.hypothesis: Scaling approach dominates over LSTM vs. Bi-LSTM choice
hypotheses.result: Supported: variable-scaling FIF consistently outperformed constant-scaling across both architectures

title: A novel hybrid intelligent optimization strategy for multi-objective trajectory planning of robotic arms in precision assembly scenarios
task: Multi-objective trajectory planning for precision robotic assembly via CEMOPSO
key_results: CEMOPSO improved assembly efficiency by 15.2%, reduced energy consumption by 20.4%, decreased impact by 26.4% vs. traditional MOPSO on pyrotechnic grain assembly
comments: Engineering validation is strong, but the comparison baseline (standard MOPSO) and specific performance metrics on simulated vs. real assembly are not fully detailed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Chebyshev mapping and evolutionary elimination improve MOPSO exploration and constraint handling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: CEMOPSO achieved 15.2% efficiency gain, 20.4% energy reduction, 26.4% impact reduction

title: Investigation of vorticity and secondary flow strength near the protected bridge pier in a sharp bend
task: Characterize vorticity and secondary flow dynamics around a bridge pier in a 180° bend channel
key_results: Peak vorticity observed at 84° section with 12 mm collar thickness
Increasing collar thickness from 0.06b to 0.24b reduced peak secondary flow strength by ~30%
Maximum tangential velocity near convex bank at water surface
comments: Field-validated experimental study with practical implications for pier design, though the mechanism linking collar thickness to secondary flow suppression could benefit from theoretical modeling.

model_io.model: 180° bend channel with oblong pier and adjustable collar
outputs: secondary flow strength at multiple bend sections (70°, 80°, 84°)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Thicker collar reduces secondary circulation strength in sharp bends
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 30% reduction in peak secondary flow strength from 3 mm to 12 mm collar

hypotheses.hypothesis: Secondary flow strength varies non-monotonically along bend trajectory
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Decline observed 70–80°, followed by increase thereafter
